annotations.annotation_text: Page 464 opens Book 3, Chapter 2 ("Jaun's Sermon") during the Age of Men phase. This passage continues Jaun (Shaun) preaching to the twenty-nine girls, the Ondt and the Gracehoper fable, departure and farewell, featuring Jaun/Shaun, Issy, the Rainbow Girls. The nocturnal dream-narrative layers Dublin topography, world mythology, and linguistic alchemy into polysemic prose.
sources: Campbell, Joseph and Robinson, Henry Morton. A Skeleton Key to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/skeletonkeytofin00camp
McHugh, Roland. Annotations to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/annotationstofin0000mchu_h5g8
Gordon, John. Finnegans Wake: A Plot Summary. https://johngordonfinnegan.weebly.com
JJDA: Finnegans Wake Genetic Edition. https://jjda.ie

annotations.annotation_text: Mid-page polysemic node on page 464 ("Jaun's Sermon"): Joyce weaves multilingual puns across 60+ languages — etymological roots from the Contemporary Literature Press lexicons (Romanian, Scandinavian, Slavic, Classical) intersect with local Dublin speech rhythms. The Age of Men dream-logic transforms ordinary syntax into a palimpsest of global literary and mythic references.
sources: Tindall, William York. A Reader's Guide to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/readersguidetofi00tind
Contemporary Literature Press: Multilingual Lexicons for FW. https://editura.mttlc.ro
Atherton, James S. The Books at the Wake. https://archive.org/details/booksatwake0000athe

annotations.annotation_text: Fall/resurrection motif "wall" on page 464 ("Jaun's Sermon"): Tim Finnegan tumbling from his ladder, Humpty Dumpty shattering from the wall, Adam falling in Eden — all converge within Jaun (Shaun) preaching to the twenty-nine girls, the Ondt and the Gracehoper fable, departure and farewell. The comic-cosmic Fall during the Age of Men phase demands its counterpart: resurrection through the whiskey-splash of the water of life (uisce beatha).
sources: The Ballad of Tim Finnegan's Wake. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finnegan%27s_Wake
Atherton, James S. The Books at the Wake. https://archive.org/details/booksatwake0000athe
Opie, Iona and Peter. The Oxford Dictionary of Nursery Rhymes. https://archive.org/details/oxforddictionary0000unse_m4u1
